summary: Preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload
details: The package's npm preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime binary from GitHub releases (bun-v1.3.13) for the detected OS/arch/libc, extracts it, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727 KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with shuffled string/opcode arrays and mangled identifiers whose contents are not statically inspectable. setup.mjs performs host fingerprinting before selecting the payload variant, calling `ldd --version` and reading `/etc/os-release` to detect musl/Alpine and branching on `process.platform`/`process.arch` to pick a matching Bun build (e.g. `bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline`). The advertised purpose of the package is a stylelint configuration, which has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime or execute an opaque bundled payload at install time. The combination of preinstall auto-execution, an alternate runtime used to bypass Node-based scanners, host fingerprinting to stage a per-platform payload, and heavy obfuscation of the executed sibling is the canonical shape of an install-time dropper against the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
